pointers.sentence: `MigrationAutodetector._prepare_field_lists` turns the comparison of fields into arithmetic on sets (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._prepare_field_lists`).

`MigrationAutodetector._generate_through_model_map`, called next, is for models that are deleted: it notes which field of the from-state uses each model named by a `through=`, and such a model's deletion is made to wait for that field's removal (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_through_model_map`).

`MigrationAutodetector.create_renamed_fields` finds each pair that could be a rename and has the questioner decide (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.create_renamed_fields`).

The operation is written later, by `MigrationAutodetector.generate_renamed_fields`: a `RenameField` with the model's name and the two field names (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_renamed_fields`).

`MigrationAutodetector.generate_removed_fields` writes a `RemoveField` for each key in the old set alone, and `MigrationAutodetector.generate_added_fields` an `AddField` for each in the new set alone (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_removed_field`, `django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_added_field`).

`MigrationAutodetector.generate_removed_fields` writes a `RemoveField` for each key in the old set alone, and `MigrationAutodetector.generate_added_fields` an `AddField` for each in the new set alone (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_removed_field`, `django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_added_field`).

A `RemoveField` waits, among the operations on its model, for an `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` that orders by anything but the field and for every `AlterUniqueTogether`, `RemoveIndex` and `RemoveConstraint`, each of which may take away a use of the field (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.check_dependency`).

`_generate_added_field` asks for none where the field is null, has a default or a `db_default`, is many-to-many, or is blank and of a class that allows empty strings (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.empty_strings_allowed`); nor for a `DateField`, `DateTimeField` or `TimeField` with `auto_now`, an `AutoField`, `SmallAutoField` or `BigAutoField`, or a field of a model that is not managed.

For each key in both sets, `MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields` fetches the two fields, the old one under the names the from-state has for the model and the field, and compares what they deconstruct to (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields`).

A field that was null and is no longer, has no default and no `db_default`, is not many-to-many and is on a managed model leaves the rows that hold null without a value, and `MigrationQuestioner.ask_not_null_alteration` is asked for one: unless the answer is `NOT_PROVIDED`, which leaves the rows to the developer, it becomes the default of a clone, with `preserve_default=False` (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:NOT_PROVIDED`).

`MigrationAutodetector.create_altered_indexes` works out three lists for each kept model, from the `"indexes"` of its two model states, and keeps them in `MigrationAutodetector.altered_indexes` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.create_altered_indexes`).

An index of the to-state that equals none of the from-state's is added, and one of the from-state's that equals none of the to-state's is removed; two indexes are equal when they are of one class and deconstruct alike, name included (`django/db/models/indexes.py:Index.__eq__`).

`MigrationAutodetector.create_altered_constraints` works out three lists for each kept model, from the `"constraints"` of its two model states: constraints added, removed and altered (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.create_altered_constraints`).

That method deconstructs both, takes out of each the arguments its class lists in `BaseConstraint.non_db_attrs`, which are `violation_error_code` and `violation_error_message`, and answers whether what is left differs (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._constraint_should_be_dropped_and_recreated`).

`MigrationAutodetector._get_altered_foo_together_operations` yields, for each kept model whose value differs, the old value and the new as sets of tuples (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._get_altered_foo_together_operations`).

Before fields are removed, `MigrationAutodetector.generate_removed_altered_unique_together` writes an `AlterUniqueTogether` to the entries both values have, where the old value had any (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_removed_altered_foo_together`).

After fields are added and altered, `MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_unique_together` writes one to the whole new value, where that has an entry the first did not keep (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._generate_altered_foo_together`).

The first step is there so that an entry which is to go has gone before fields are removed and altered (`tests/migrations/test_autodetector.py:AutodetectorTests.test_alter_field_and_unique_together`).

`MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_order_with_respect_to` compares the option `order_with_respect_to` in the two model states, and where it differs writes an `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` to the new value (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_order_with_respect_to`).
